title: Levedia and Etelköz
fact_summary: Two earlier homes of the Hungarians named in the Byzantine chapter on them. Where exactly they lay is not settled by the sources read so far.

claims.text: The chapter says the Turks (Hungarians) once lived near Khazaria in a place “named Levedia after their first voivode” (“melyet elsô vajdájuk nevérôl Levediának neveznek”).

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: Tóth summarises the chapter as saying that the western part of the people settled in Etelköz, the land of “Atelkuzu”, under Levedi's leadership.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Tóth's own summary of the chapter.

claims.text: The chapter places the election of the prince, Árpád, in Etelköz.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: The story of the two settlements comes from two separate reports joined in chapter 38, each with its own settlement, Khazar episode and Pecheneg attack.
claims.certainty_reason: Argued by one tier B study.

open_questions.text: Where were Levedia and Etelköz? No pin is drawn until a checked source places them.
